g.text: N1 [Context]
Diffusion drives generative modelling progress
Generative modelling for continuous data modalities — like images, video,
and audio — has advanced rapidly, propelled by improvements in
diffusion-based approaches.
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=0) Generative modelling for continuous data modalities — like images, video, and audio — has advanced rapidly, propelled by improvements in diffusion-based approaches.

g.text: N2 [Context]
Commercial AI image generation widespread
Many companies now offer easy access to AI-generated bespoke image content.
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=0) Many companies now offer easy access to AI-generated bespoke image content.

g.text: N3 [Context]
Need to understand training-data influence
However, the use of these models for commercial purposes creates a need for
understanding how the training data influences their outputs.
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=0) However, the use of these models for commercial purposes creates a need for understanding how the training data influences their outputs.

g.text: N4 [Context]
Need to identify/remove harmful training data
In cases where the model's outputs are undesirable, it is useful to be able
to identify, and possibly remove, the training data instances responsible
for those outputs.
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=0) In cases where the model's outputs are undesirable, it is useful to be able to identify, and possibly remove, the training data instances responsible for those outputs.

g.text: N5 [Context]
Copyright works in training corpora raise concerns
Furthermore, as copyrighted works often make up a significant part of the
training corpora of these models (Schuhmann et al., 2022), concerns about
the extent to which individual copyright owners' works influence the
generated samples…
g.title: N5 [Context] (cites=1) Furthermore, as copyrighted works often make up a significant part of the training corpora of these models (Schuhmann et al., 2022), concerns about the extent to which individual copyright owners' works influence the generated samples arise.

g.text: N6 [Context]
Lawsuits over 'copyright infringement as a service'
Some already characterise what these companies offer as “copyright
infringement as a service” (Saveri & Butterick, 2023a), which has caused a
flurry of high-profile lawsuits Saveri & Butterick (2023a;b).
g.title: N6 [Context] (cites=2) Some already characterise what these companies offer as “copyright infringement as a service” (Saveri & Butterick, 2023a), which has caused a flurry of high-profile lawsuits Saveri & Butterick (2023a;b).

g.text: N7 [Context]
Motivates data attribution tools
This motivates exploring tools for data attribution that might be able to
quantify how each group of training data points influences the models'
outputs.
g.title: N7 [Context] (cites=0) This motivates exploring tools for data attribution that might be able to quantify how each group of training data points influences the models' outputs.

g.text: N8 [Prior_Work : ANCHOR]
Influence functions: a known attribution tool
Influence functions (Koh & Liang, 2017b; Bae et al.,
2022) offer precisely such a tool.
g.title: N8 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) Influence functions (Koh & Liang, 2017b; Bae et al., 2022) offer precisely such a tool.

g.text: N9 [Prior_Work]
IFs answer the leave-out counterfactual
By approximating the answer to the question, “If the model was
trained with some of the data excluded, what would its output
be?”, they can help finding data points most responsible for a low
loss on an example, or a high probability of…
g.title: N9 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) By approximating the answer to the question, “If the model was trained with some of the data excluded, what would its output be?”, they can help finding data points most responsible for a low loss on an example, or a high probability of generating a particular example.

g.text: N10 [Limitation]
Not yet scalable for diffusion
However, they have yet to be scalably adapted to the general
diffusion modelling setting.
g.title: N10 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, they have yet to be scalably adapted to the general diffusion modelling setting.

g.text: N11 [Prior_Work]
IFs locally approximate loss-landscape change
Influence functions work by locally approximating how
the loss landscape would change if some of the training
data points were down-weighted in the training loss
(illustrated in Figure 4).
g.title: N11 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) Influence functions work by locally approximating how the loss landscape would change if some of the training data points were down-weighted in the training loss (illustrated in Figure 4).

g.text: N12 [Prior_Work]
IFs predict optimum + parameter changes
Consequently, this enables prediction for how the (local) optimum
of the training loss would change, and how that change in the
parameters would affect a measurement of interest (e.g., loss on a
particular example).
g.title: N12 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) Consequently, this enables prediction for how the (local) optimum of the training loss would change, and how that change in the parameters would affect a measurement of interest (e.g., loss on a particular example).

g.text: N13 [Prior_Work]
Extrapolate to full-removal estimate
By extrapolating this prediction, one can estimate what would happen if the
data points were fully removed from the training set.
g.title: N13 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) By extrapolating this prediction, one can estimate what would happen if the data points were fully removed from the training set.

g.text: N14 [Limitation]
Hessian inversion is expensive
However, to locally approximate the shape of the loss landscape,
influence functions require computing and inverting the Hessian of
the training loss, which is computationally expensive.
g.title: N14 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, to locally approximate the shape of the loss landscape, influence functions require computing and inverting the Hessian of the training loss, which is computationally expensive.

g.text: N15 [Prior_Work]
GGN: common Hessian approximation
One common approximation of the training loss's Hessian
is the generalised Gauss-Newton matrix (GGN,
Schraudolph, 2002; Martens, 2020).
g.title: N15 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) One common approximation of the training loss's Hessian is the generalised Gauss-Newton matrix (GGN, Schraudolph, 2002; Martens, 2020).

g.text: N16 [Limitation]
GGN not formulated for diffusion objective
The GGN has not been clearly formulated for the diffusion
modelling objective before and cannot be uniquely determined based
on its general definition.
g.title: N16 [Limitation] (cites=0) The GGN has not been clearly formulated for the diffusion modelling objective before and cannot be uniquely determined based on its general definition.

g.text: N17 [Limitation]
GGN itself needs further approximation
Moreover, to compute and store a GGN for large neural networks further
approximations are necessary.
g.title: N17 [Limitation] (cites=0) Moreover, to compute and store a GGN for large neural networks further approximations are necessary.

g.text: N18 [Method]
Propose K-FAC / EK-FAC for GGN
We propose using Kronecker-Factored Approximate Curvature (K-FAC,
Heskes, 2000; Martens & Grosse, 2015) and its variant
eigenvalue-corrected K-FAC (George et al., 2018, EK-FAC) to
approximate the GGN.
g.title: N18 [Method] (cites=3) We propose using Kronecker-Factored Approximate Curvature (K-FAC, Heskes, 2000; Martens & Grosse, 2015) and its variant eigenvalue-corrected K-FAC (George et al., 2018, EK-FAC) to approximate the GGN.

g.text: N19 [Prior_Work]
Kwon et al.: K-FAC seen as non-applicable
It is not commonly known how to apply it to neural
network architectures used in diffusion models; for
example, Kwon et al. (2023) resort to alternative
Hessian approximation methods because “[K-FAC] might…
g.title: N19 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) It is not commonly known how to apply it to neural network architectures used in diffusion models; for example, Kwon et al. (2023) resort to alternative Hessian approximation methods because “[K-FAC] might not be applicable to general deep neural network models as it highly depends on the model architecture”.

g.text: N20 [Method]
K-FAC applies to diffusion architectures
However, based on recent work, it is indeed clear that it can be
applied to architectures used in diffusion models (Grosse &
Martens, 2016; Eschenhagen et al., 2023), which typically combine
linear layers, convolutions, and attention (Ho…
g.title: N20 [Method] (cites=3) However, based on recent work, it is indeed clear that it can be applied to architectures used in diffusion models (Grosse & Martens, 2016; Eschenhagen et al., 2023), which typically combine linear layers, convolutions, and attention (Ho et al., 2020).

g.text: N21 [Method]
Scalable IF for diffusion via (E)K-FAC GGN
In this work, we describe a scalable approach to influence function-based
approximations for data attribution in diffusion models, using (E)K-FAC
approximation of GGNs as Hessian approximations.
g.title: N21 [Method] (cites=0) In this work, we describe a scalable approach to influence function-based approximations for data attribution in diffusion models, using (E)K-FAC approximation of GGNs as Hessian approximations.

g.text: N22 [Method]
Articulate IF design space; unify prior methods
We articulate a design space based on influence functions, unify previous
methods for data attribution in diffusion models (Georgiev et al., 2023;
Zheng et al., 2024) through our framework, and argue for the design choices
that distinguish…
g.title: N22 [Method] (cites=2) We articulate a design space based on influence functions, unify previous methods for data attribution in diffusion models (Georgiev et al., 2023; Zheng et al., 2024) through our framework, and argue for the design choices that distinguish our method from previous ones.

g.text: N23 [Method]
GGN is a key design choice
One important design choice is the GGN used as the Hessian approximation.
g.title: N23 [Method] (cites=0) One important design choice is the GGN used as the Hessian approximation.

g.text: N23a [Method]
Formulate diffusion-specific GGN matrices
We formulate different GGN matrices for the diffusion modelling objective
and discuss their implicit assumptions.
g.title: N23a [Method] (cites=0) We formulate different GGN matrices for the diffusion modelling objective and discuss their implicit assumptions.

g.text: N24 [Result]
Outperforms prior attribution on LDS / retraining
We empirically ablate variations of the GGN approximation and other design
choices in our framework and show that our proposed method outperforms the
existing data attribution methods for diffusion models as measured by common
data…
g.title: N24 [Result] (cites=1) We empirically ablate variations of the GGN approximation and other design choices in our framework and show that our proposed method outperforms the existing data attribution methods for diffusion models as measured by common data attribution metrics like the Linear Datamodeling Score (Park et al., 2023) or retraining without top influences.

g.text: N25 [Contribution]
Empirical observations challenge IF understanding
Finally, we also discuss interesting empirical observations that challenge
our current understanding of influence functions in the context of diffusion
models.
g.title: N25 [Contribution] (cites=0) Finally, we also discuss interesting empirical observations that challenge our current understanding of influence functions in the context of diffusion models.

consequence (Therefore)
evidence (→ Result/Proof)
